Potential Shared Solutions: Resilience Hubs as a shared solution can provide many resources to individuals during power outages. Allowing priority admission to those with life- sustaining devices will ensure those individuals can maintain health and safety until power is restored. Rationale: In the event of a power outage, individuals who rely on powered medical devices are particularly vulnerable and need to be prioritized in emergency preparedness efforts. Medical devices such as ventilators, oxygen concentrators, dialysis machines, and CPAPs are crucial for the daily health and well-being of many individuals. Without power, these devices cannot function, potentially putting lives at risk. A community must work to ensure that these individuals have plans in place to maintain the operation of their medical devices and receive the support they need during prolonged grid outages. One of the most critical preparedness actions is ensuring that individuals with powered medical devices have access to backup power. This can be accomplished through the use of generators, uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), or portable power banks, depending on the device's power requirements. Emergency managers should encourage individuals to assess the capacity of their medical devices and match it with the appropriate backup power sources. Moreover, it is essential that backup power systems are tested regularly to ensure they are in working order. In addition, individuals should be instructed to have extra fuel or batteries available to sustain these devices for extended periods, especially during long-term power outages. Communication is another key element and may include individuals using medical devices registering with local emergency services and/or the electric utility, to ensure that they can be prioritized for assistance in the event of a power failure. Establishing a notification system can also make sure individuals receive early warnings of potential outages, so they can take proactive measures to safeguard their health and device functionality. It is important for these systems to be accessible and reliable, with regular checks to ensure they are functioning and reaching those who need them. Doctors, home healthcare providers, and medical supply companies should be part of the conversation when crafting individualized emergency preparedness strategies for those who use powered medical devices. These professionals can provide guidance on maintaining and using medical equipment in the event of a power outage, including recommendations on safe usage, device alternatives, or steps to take should the power go out unexpectedly. Healthcare providers should also ensure their patients have up-to-date contact information and a plan for quickly accessing medical care if needed during a crisis.
